description:
Bilge & Fire System Schematic for a Southern Wind yacht, drawing no. 108-01-520-001, sheets 1/1, dated 15 Jun 2022, revision B dated 30 Sep 2022 (“ADDED ESS ENCLOSURE BILGE PICKUP”). The upper half is a general arrangement showing hull zones, fire hydrants, pumps, maximum fire-hose reach, and bilge/fire pipe routing. The lower half is the flow schematic.

FLOW PATHS AND CONNECTIONS
1) Main bilge line (cyan, metallic pipe): longitudinal line between aft and forward stowage. At each end it terminates at a fire hose/nozzle assembly in stowage. Branches connect bilge pickups/sumps, engine-room bilge system, mast area sump, ESS enclosure, main bilge pump, and anti-siphon discharge. Arrowheads show longitudinal flow generally toward the main bilge pumping/discharge arrangement on the starboard/right side, with local suction branches rising from sumps into the main line.
2) Fire line (red/pink, metallic pipe): longitudinal fire main supplied through labeled FIRE LINE SEAWATER SUPPLY branches. Fire hydrants/nozzles are shown at aft and forward stowage. Main/auxiliary fire pumps draw from seawater arrangements and discharge into the fire main; local branches and isolating valves divide sections.
3) Lazarette/tender-garage branch: tender-garage pickup passes through seater strainer 005-01 and valves to diesel fire pump 002-01. A fresh-water priming line is cross-referenced to drawing 108-01-510-001. Diesel fire pump discharge ties into the fire main; bilge-overboard branch is shown. Lazarette sump pickup 005-01 feeds through valve 010-01 to the cyan main bilge line. Bilge alarm 007-01 is shown at the lazarette sump.
4) Midship sump: pickups 006-02 and 006-03 feed the cyan main bilge line through branch isolation/check-valve arrangements; bilge alarm 007-02 is shown.
5) Engine room: cyan main bilge line traverses engine room. Engine-room sump pickups 006-04 and 006-05 connect through valves to the suction arrangement; bilge alarms 007-03 and 025-02/025-03 are shown. A dedicated engine-room auxiliary bilge pump 003-02 is associated with oily bilge filter 004-01 and portable-oil-storage-tank connections 021-01 and 021-03. A FLEX SUCTION HOSE CONNECTION 021-01 is shown. Raw-water pump/sea-chest supply and overboard wet-exhaust water-separation references are shown to other drawings.
6) Mast area: mast area sump pickup 006-06 connects to main bilge line through valve 007-04. Two deck-drain/locker drain paths are shown, each noted “MIN. 800mm ABOVE DWL,” joining below DWL. Mast area bilge pump 003-01 draws via mast aux bilge pump suction manifold and valves 026-01/026-02, with portable-oil-storage-tank connection 021-03 and flex suction hose connection 021-01. Bilge alarm 025-04 and auxiliary-pump alarm 025-05 are shown.
7) ESS enclosure: pickup 006-08 and bilge alarm 007-06 are shown. A coolant-leak alarm is also marked. The ESS pickup joins the mast-area auxiliary suction manifold through a branch controlled by valve 026-02.
8) Main bilge pump and overboard: main bilge pump 003-01 draws through seawater strainer 005-02 and associated valves. Its discharge is routed to an anti-siphon manifold identified as 700mm ABOVE DWL, then to a bilge overboard outlet. A branch includes electric fire pump 002-02 and fire-main connection. Breaker to run into starboard engine-room vent box is cross-referenced to drawing 108-01-508-001.
9) Sail locker sump: pickup 006-08 with bilge alarm 007-05 connects to the main bilge line via local branch; forward-stowage hose/nozzle assembly is at the far right.

ISOLATION / CROSSOVERS
- Numerous labeled 2-way ball valves (010 series and others) isolate sump pickup branches, pump suctions/discharges, fire-main sections, seawater supply branches, and overboard branches. Valve status text NO/NC is printed beside many valves.
- Longitudinal fire main and main bilge main are sectioned at hull/fire boundaries identified by letters L, G, F, E, C, B, A.
- Fire-line seawater-supply tie-ins provide cross-connections into the red fire main near both ends.
- The mast auxiliary bilge suction manifold is a crossover selector joining mast-area/ESS and portable/flex suction branches to the mast auxiliary bilge pump.
- The anti-siphon manifold prevents siphoning on the main bilge discharge and is explicitly located 700 mm above design waterline.
- The diesel fire pump tender-garage suction arrangement includes a manual pull-start note and fresh-water priming crossover.

PRINTED DATA / RATINGS
Pump data table:
- MAIN BILGE PUMP: Feit VA 408 (24V DC), flow rate 300 l/min (18 m³/h), power 0.75 kW, max head 17 m.
- ELECTRIC FIRE PUMP: Gianneschi ACB431 (24V DC), flow rate 230 l/min (13.8 m³/h), power 1.5 kW, max head 30 m.
- DIESEL FIRE PUMP: Aussen Pumps LF48 (Yanmar YD510), flow rate 715 l/min (42.9 m³/h), power 5.6 kW, max head 37 m.
- MAIN ENGINE RAW WATER PUMP: Cummins QSB4.5 Engine Pump, flow rate 195 l/min (11.7 m³/h); power/head not stated.
- AUXILIARY BILGE PUMP: Whale Gulper 320 (24V DC), flow rate 19 l/min (1.1 m³/h), power 0.1 kW, max head 3 m.
Other printed ratings/details:
- Fire hose: ISO 15540 fire resistant.
- Fire hose nominal length: 15 m + 3 m.
- Maximum reach annotations: 15 m fire hose from forward hydrant and 18 m fire hose aft hydrant.
- Engine-room vent/locker drains: minimum 800 mm above DWL.
- Anti-siphon manifold: 700 mm above DWL.
- Lazarette shaded area marked AREA: 12.8 m².

CROSS-REFERENCES
- Fire line in port sheet: REF: DWG 108-01-515-003.
- Fresh-water supply/priming line: REF: DWG 108-01-510-001.
- From sea chest supply: REF: DWG 108-01-515-003.
- Overboard wet exhaust water separation: REF: DWG 108-01-515-001.
- Breaker to run into STBD E-R vent box: REF: DWG 108-01-508-001.

STANDARD/DRAWING NOTES
- To be read in conjunction with separate drawing 108-01-520-002 BILGE & FIRE SYSTEM OPERATING MODES.
- All thru-hull valve sizes are detailed in drawing 108-01-504-002 THRU-HULL BELOW DWL.
- Do not scale; dimensions in millimeters unless otherwise indicated; break all sharp edges of metal parts; all parts weights to be noted after manufacturing; do not measure off drawing; ask drawing office for missing information.
